body.statement: For every finite acquired collection \(E_0\) on which the full correctly typed unconditional CTFIDU\({}^{+}(G,Q,\mathcal R(E_0))\) procedure accepts, there exists a uniform certificate \(E\) using only protocols and slices represented in \(E_0\), with \(\operatorname{Cost}(E)\le\operatorname{Cost}(E_0)\), at most one source-slice record per target factor \(C_j\), at most \(k\) nonempty records, and at most \(k\) distinct protocols. For each factor, its selected protocol, slice, labelled source, and ancestor-district transcript schema succeed simultaneously for every assignment and induced equality type in \(\Omega_j\). Conversely, every uniform certificate accepted by \(\operatorname{Acc}\) induces a complete accepting CTFIDU\({}^{+}\) run on \(\mathcal R(E)\).
body.justification: This quantifier-exchange theorem is the load-bearing bridge from complete fixed-source identification to a compact acquisition certificate and is directly stress-tested by the finite equality-type search.
body.gap: Raghavan and Bareinboim (2026), Algorithm 2 and Appendix E, establish completeness for concrete labelled queries and fixed regimes; they do not prove that one selected source and restriction schema remain valid across every free assignment and equality type of a target factor.
body.consumer: The theorem limits paid acquisitions and auditable source transcripts by the number of target districts rather than the number of value assignments.
